clue.text: Church about to capture portent with insecticide

indicators.note: to capture means the first piece holds the second inside it

parts.note: RE, Latin for 'in the matter of', means about

explanation.surface: A clergyman is about to seize an ominous sign along with some bug spray.
explanation.definitionFit: Chromene is an organic compound whose derivatives are used as insect-killing agents.

clue.text: Crater here buried in decadence

indicators.note: buried in says the letters lie concealed within the next word

explanation.surface: A volcanic crater lies deep beneath a scene of decadence.
explanation.walkthrough: The city of Aden is built inside the crater of an extinct volcano, which is why 'Crater here' defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: Aden in Yemen is famously set within an old volcanic crater, so it is a place where a crater is.

clue.text: Non-discriminatory higher education congress

explanation.surface: A university conference that welcomes everyone regardless of background.
explanation.definitionFit: Unisex things are designed for both men and women alike, not discriminating between them.

clue.text: Kentish king only too ready to dish it out here

definitions.text: ready to dish it out here

parts.note: Kent is in the south-east of England, abbreviated SE
R is short for rex, Latin for king
only too, as in 'only too pleased', means very

explanation.surface: An old monarch of Kent is all too eager to hand out food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kentish king' looks like one historical figure, but it splits into SE, for Kent's south-eastern corner of England, and R.
explanation.definitionFit: A servery is a counter or room where prepared food is served out to diners.

clue.text: Name entered against one good German author

parts.note: V, short for versus, means against

indicators.note: entered means the first-named letter goes inside the word that follows

parts.note: gut is the German word for good

explanation.surface: A name is entered on the list against a single worthy German writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Kurt Vonnegut was an American novelist, the writer of Slaughterhouse-Five.

clue.text: Lock many into the Seigneur's domain; it should have a pronounced effect

definitions.text: it should have a pronounced effect

indicators.note: into means these pieces are placed inside the next one

parts.note: the Channel Island of Sark has long been ruled by its feudal lord, the Seigneur
a lock of hair is a tress
M, the Roman numeral for a thousand, stands for many

explanation.surface: A feudal lord locks up many people in his territory, which ought to make a big impression.
explanation.walkthrough: Sark, a tiny Channel Island, was governed by a hereditary Seigneur, so 'the Seigneur's domain' is SARK.
explanation.definitionFit: A mark showing which syllable is stressed indicates how a word is pronounced, punning on pronounced as marked.

clue.text: Dickensian whose vine became wine

parts.note: a Dickens character in The Pickwick Papers famously swaps the sounds of v and w in his Cockney speech

explanation.walkthrough: Sam, Mr Pickwick's servant, says 'wery' for 'very' and 'vell' for 'well', so a vine in his mouth becomes a wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Sam is the Cockney manservant of Mr Pickwick in Dickens's first novel, known for his v-w swaps.

clue.text: Confess! The evil head event involved 21's performance

indicators.note: involved means twisted up together, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Own up! The wicked leader's occasion was a performance by Salome.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 is Salome, whose seductive dance before Herod won her the head of John the Baptist; the evil head and the confession fit that story.
explanation.definitionFit: In Wilde's play and Strauss's opera, Salome performs this striptease dance before Herod.

clue.text: See 8
Jordan's precursor went topless after 8 9 11

parts.note: the forerunner who baptised in the River Jordan was beheaded after Salome's dance

explanation.walkthrough: 'Went topless' sounds like stripping, but here it means losing his head, the reward Salome asked for after her dance.
explanation.definitionFit: This prophet baptised Jesus in the Jordan and was called his forerunner, later beheaded at Salome's request.

clue.text: See 1
Wildly met relations outside with explosive outcome

indicators.note: outside means the first piece wraps round the second
wildly means the letters of the word met are thrown about

explanation.surface: Two people met and had a passionate fling that ended with a bang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relations' reads as family members, but it means sexual relations; 'Wildly' scrambles the meeting into the middle of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Semtex is a plastic explosive, so its result is a blast.

clue.text: See 10
Like Bognor's attempt to enter the lists here

parts.note: the seaside town Bognor Regis carries the royal suffix Regis, Latin for 'of the king'

explanation.surface: A seaside town makes a bid to join a jousting tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: Bognor Regis is an English seaside resort on the south coast. 'Enter the lists' suggests jousting, but a registry is where entries are made in lists or registers.
explanation.definitionFit: A registry is an office where official registers are kept and records written into them.

clue.text: Well woman? That's novel!

definitions.meaning: in Genesis, Isaac's future wife is found drawing water at a well
a Daphne du Maurier novel of 1938 bears this title

explanation.walkthrough: 'Well woman' suggests a healthy woman or a health clinic, but it means the biblical woman met at a well.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical bride of Isaac and the title of du Maurier's novel share the same name.

clue.text: Native Americans looking good in trousers

indicators.note: in means the second piece sits inside the first

parts.note: OK means all right, looking good

explanation.surface: Some Native Americans look smart wearing casual trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chinook are a Native American people of the Pacific Northwest.

clue.text: Get out of Germany in ways of 21's creator

indicators.note: in means the German word is placed inside the ways

parts.note: ST is short for street, so streets or ways are STS
raus is German for get out

explanation.surface: Fleeing Germany by various routes, the composer of Salome escaped.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 is Salome; Richard Strauss composed the opera Salome in 1905.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Strauss wrote the opera Salome, so he is its composer.

clue.text: Bar progress along this way east?

definitions.text: Bar progress along this way east?

parts.words: Bar progress along this way east?
parts.note: a barrister progresses by becoming a QC, or taking silk, and this historic trade route led east

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' seems to mean block, but it is the legal profession: a barrister's road to promotion leads to silk.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient overland trade route linking China to the West carried silk east to west.

clue.text: Squaddies' song of gal the army MOs list "dubious"

indicators.note: dubious means doubtful or shaky, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: The army doctors call a soldiers' ditty about a girl questionable.
explanation.walkthrough: Squaddies are British slang for private soldiers; this bawdy song about Salome was sung in the trenches.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a rude marching song popular among British soldiers in the World Wars.

clue.text: Lamb-like orientals utter his rubbish

parts.note: E stands for east or eastern, so orientals are Es

indicators.note: rubbish means the word his is trashed and its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: Eastern people speak dismissively of his nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lamb' is not the animal but Charles Lamb, the English writer famous for his Essays of Elia.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing in the style of Charles Lamb, an essayist, is in the manner of an essay.

clue.text: See 19
Nothing injected in joint of African beef

indicators.note: injected in means the first piece is pushed inside the second

explanation.surface: No hormones were put into a cut of meat from Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Ankole cattle, with huge horns, are an East African breed raised for meat.

clue.text: Road mending with primitive zeal

indicators.note: mending means repairing, so the letters of road are reworked

parts.note: ur- is a prefix meaning original or primitive

explanation.surface: Fixing the road was done with basic enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardour is intense passion or enthusiasm, a close synonym of zeal.

clue.text: Maladroit and hardly even-handed

definitions.meaning: playfully, something that is level by foot rather than by hand

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes 'even-handed' literally: feet that are flat are even, but that is not even hands.
explanation.definitionFit: Being caught flat-footed means being clumsy or unprepared, and flat feet are level ones.

clue.text: See 19
Apropos at leaving Cobbett's London with girl

indicators.note: leaving means these letters depart from the longer phrase

parts.note: William Cobbett famously called London 'the Great Wen', a wen being a swollen growth

explanation.surface: Concerning a girl who left the capital described by Cobbett.
explanation.walkthrough: William Cobbett, a 19th-century English writer, called London the Great Wen; removing RE and AT from GREATWEN leaves the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Gwen is a girl's name, short for Gwendolen.

clue.text: Type of Greek fire picked up in supermarkets?

indicators.note: picked up means heard, as by a microphone, so the sound counts

parts.note: mu is a Greek letter, a piece of Greek type; to fire someone is to sack them

explanation.surface: A kind of ancient incendiary weapon was found in grocery stores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek fire' was a Byzantine incendiary weapon, but here it splits into MU and SACK, which said together sound like the background music.
explanation.definitionFit: Bland piped background music is what shoppers hear playing in supermarkets.

clue.text: Forget-me-not for use in amore perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the combined letters may be arranged differently

explanation.surface: A forget-me-not is a token one might use in love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amore' is Italian for love, giving the surface its romance; 'perhaps' tells the solver the letters of the two words can be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Mouse-ear is a common name for plants including the forget-me-not, from their small furry leaves.
